headline: Solid core growth overshadowed by a one-time tax windfall
summary_short: Yum! Brands' Q2 FY2026 revenue rose to $2,169M (+5.3% q/q, +12.3% y/y) on Taco Bell and KFC same-store sales growth, while diluted EPS jumped to $3.08 as one-time tax benefits tied to the planned Pizza Hut sale pushed net income to $853M.
summary_long: Revenue rose 5.3% q/q and 12.3% y/y to $2,169M on Taco Bell (+7% same-store) and KFC (+2% same-store) growth and unit expansion; Pizza Hut sales were flat. Operating income grew a slower 1.7% q/q as $44M of Pizza Hut strategic-review charges and higher Hut Forward advertising offset KFC/Taco Bell gains. Net income surged to $853M and diluted EPS to $3.08 almost entirely on one-time tax benefits ($359M deferred-tax plus $91M IP-transfer) tied to June's agreements to sell Pizza Hut, expected to close August 2026. Cash fell slightly to $674M; short-term debt jumped as revolver/Term Loan A borrowings were reclassified current; shareholders' deficit narrowed to -$7,107M.

drivers.explanation: Net income and EPS growth are driven almost entirely by one-time tax benefits from June 2026's definitive agreements to sell Pizza Hut, not by operating performance improvement.
Reflects a $359M deferred-tax benefit from tax basis recognized on entering Pizza Hut sale agreements, plus $91M from an intra-entity IP transfer tied to the Pizza Hut reorganization.

Special Items added $1.46 of the $3.08 diluted EPS, almost entirely the Pizza Hut-sale-related tax benefits described above rather than operating EPS excluding Special Items, which rose a smaller 12%.
Driven by Taco Bell same-store sales growth of 7% and KFC same-store sales growth of 2%, plus unit growth and restaurant acquisitions from franchisees; Pizza Hut system sales were roughly flat.

KFC and Taco Bell same-store sales and unit growth were partly offset by $44M of Pizza Hut strategic-options-review charges and higher Hut Forward advertising spend that cut Pizza Hut's own operating profit 12%.

Company restaurant expenses rose mainly on the Taco Bell Southeast U.S. franchisee-restaurant acquisition adding to the Company-operated cost base, plus higher labor costs and beef-commodity inflation at Taco Bell.

Term Loan A and Revolving Facility borrowings ($675M drawn) were reclassified to short-term because the $750M of Subsidiary Senior Unsecured Notes they're tied to hadn't been refinanced 91 days ahead of its June 2027 maturity.
